answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that decays only after proven honest work: cheap clones multiply, but each clone pays the same bond. Like a grove where every tree must sink roots, the stake makes mass identity farming unprofitable, because an attacker funding a thousand fake agents pays a thousand bonds. The ocean of cheap identities drains away once creating one costs more than the reward it can extract, and crystal-clear on-ledger stake history lets peers check whether an identity earned its standing or merely appeared overnight.
